SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only water vapour

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.

4. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Producers

5. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

6. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Milk souring
   D. Iron rusting

7. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.

9. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

10. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

11. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

12. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Removing all vegetation

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Glucose and oxygen

2. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

3. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

4. D — Producers

5. C — 100 °C

6. A — Ice melting to water

7. A — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

8. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.

9. D — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

10. B — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

11. B — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

12. C — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Composition of Air; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Light; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Levers as simple machines; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Slopes as simple machines; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
